edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Chronic proton-pump inhibition lowers gastric acidity, which can impair release or absorption of certain nutrients and may alter bone or magnesium handling over long exposure periods. That makes Vitamin B12 deficiency more plausible with duration-dependent use than with short courses.
edges.summary: This is one of the cleaner pharmacology edges in the set because the adverse pathway is predictable and monitoring can often reduce harm. Pooled meta-analytic evidence link long-term proton pump inhibitor use to higher risk of vitamin b12 deficiency in adults on chronic PPI therapy. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Medication benefits may still outweigh this risk. The practical implication is usually monitoring, dosing separation, or targeted supplementation rather than indiscriminate discontinuation.
